---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

When Positron does not start for a student, the cause is almost always in one of
four places: the launcher extension in the user environment, the license file, the
install itself, which covers architecture and version, or, on Positron Server
2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2, the Hub verifier service. This page is organized by
symptom.

## Where to look first

Most answers are in the logs.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### TLJH / systemd
```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
# Full Hub log, which covers spawn errors and service registration
journalctl -u jupyterhub --no-pager -n 200
```

### docker-compose
```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
# Hub log
docker compose logs hub

# A student's single-user container, named by `docker ps`
docker logs <jupyter-USERNAME-container>
```
:::

The single-user server log shows what `jupyter-positron-server` and
`positron-server` reported at launch. Reach it from the JupyterHub UI under the
student server, or from the spawner logs.

## The Positron tile does not appear

`jupyter-positron-server` provides the tile through `jupyter-server-proxy`, in the
**user** environment.

Check the user environment:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
/opt/tljh/user/bin/pip show jupyter-positron-server
/opt/tljh/user/bin/jupyter server extension list
```

Fixes:

- Extension missing: install it in the user environment and enable the proxy.
  ```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
  /opt/tljh/user/bin/pip install 'jupyter-positron-server>=0.0.5'
  /opt/tljh/user/bin/jupyter server extension enable --sys-prefix jupyter_server_proxy
  ```
- Installed but no tile: confirm `JSP_POSITRON_LAUNCHER_DISABLED` is not set in the
  spawner environment. Any value hides the tile.
- Restart the student server, by stopping and starting it from the JupyterHub UI.
  The extension is picked up on server start, not on Hub reload.

## The tile is there, but Positron never loads

The launcher runs, and `positron-server` fails to start.

- **`positron-server: command not found`**: `positron-server` is not on the session
  `PATH`. Confirm the spawner sets it.
  ```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
  c.Spawner.environment = {
      "PATH": "/opt/positron-server/bin:" + os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"),
  }
  ```
  In the docker template the binary is on `PATH` through the single-user image
  `ENV`, and the spawner does not override `PATH`.
- **A license error**: see the section below that matches your Positron Server
  version.

## License errors on 2026.09.0 and newer

These versions read `license.lic` from the activation directory and validate it
with the bundled `license-manager`. Check the license first:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
/opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license-manager status
```

Common failures:

- **Permission denied on the license file**: each session reads the file as the
  student, so a root-only mode such as `600` fails every session. Confirm the mode
  is `644`.
  ```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
  ls -l /opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license.lic
  chmod 644 /opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license.lic
  ```
- **License file not found**: the file must sit next to the `license-manager`
  binary, and it must be named `license.lic`. A file named `positron.lic` is not
  found.
- **Expired or altered license**: `license-manager status` reports the reason. A
  license file that exists but does not verify stops the session rather than
  falling back to anything else. Request a replacement from
  [academic-licenses@posit.co](mailto:academic-licenses@posit.co).
- **Wrong architecture directory**: `positron-server` looks under
  `resources/activation/linux/x86_64` on x64 hosts and
  `resources/activation/linux/aarch64` on arm64 hosts. A license placed in the
  other directory is not found.

::: callout-note
On these versions, `jupyter-positron-server` 0.0.5 logs a warning at launch that
neither `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` nor `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE` is
set, and that a signed token is required. Ignore that warning.
`positron-server` finds and validates the license file itself.
:::

## License errors on 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2

These versions accept a signed token only, which the Hub verifier mints. The
verifier runs as a managed JupyterHub service, so its output lands in the Hub log:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
journalctl -u jupyterhub --no-pager | grep -i positron-license
# docker: docker compose logs hub | grep -i positron-license
```

### The verifier is not running or not registered

- **No mention at all**: the service config was not loaded. Confirm that
  `jupyterhub_config.py`, or the generated `positron-license.py` in
  `jupyterhub_config.d/`, contains the `c.JupyterHub.services` block, then reload.
  ```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
  tljh-config reload
  # or: systemctl restart jupyterhub
  # docker: docker compose restart hub
  ```
- **The service starts and then dies**: confirm the command exists in the **Hub**
  environment.
  ```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
  /opt/tljh/hub/bin/pip show jupyter-positron-verifier
  ls -l /opt/tljh/hub/bin/positron-verifier
  ```
- **Port conflict** on `VERIFIER_PORT`, which defaults to `10101`: another process
  holds the port. Change `VERIFIER_PORT` and update
  `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` to match.

### Mint calls fail

- **Signing key not readable**: the verifier runs as the Hub service account and
  reads `POSITRON_MINTING_KEY_FILE`. Confirm the file exists and that account can
  read it.
  ```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
  ls -l /etc/positron/signing-key.pem   # mode 600, owned by the Hub user
  ```
- **Minting endpoint unreachable or wrong URL**:
  `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` must point at the Hub-proxied service path.
  On TLJH that is `http://127.0.0.1:10101/services/positron-license/mint`. On
  docker it is `http://hub:${VERIFIER_PORT}/services/positron-license/mint`.
- **`403` or other authorization errors from the mint call**: the service role is
  missing scopes. Confirm the `c.JupyterHub.load_roles` block grants the
  `positron-license` service `read:users`.

::: callout-note
Upgrading to Positron Server 2026.09.0 or newer removes this whole class of
failure. See
[Move an existing deployment off the verifier](get_started.qmd#move-an-existing-deployment-off-the-verifier).
:::

## Install-time failures

- **Download fails with `curl` 403 or 404**: the `POSITRON_VERSION` and
  `POSITRON_ARCH` combination does not exist on the CDN. Verify the version string
  against the [Positron releases page](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/releases),
  or download the tarball yourself and pass
  `POSITRON_TARBALL=./positron-server.tar.gz`.

## docker-compose specifics

- **The hub container exits at boot reporting a file not found or empty**: a secret
  was not placed. Copy the files into `scripts/docker/secrets/`. A missing
  bind-mount source makes Docker create an empty directory, which is why the hub
  checks at boot.
  ```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
  cp /path/to/signing-key.pem secrets/signing-key.pem
  cp /path/to/license.lic     secrets/license.lic
  docker compose up -d
  ```
- **Single-user containers fail to spawn**: build the single-user image with
  `docker compose build hub singleuser`, and confirm that its
  `jupyterhub-singleuser` version is compatible with the Hub JupyterHub version.
- **Anyone can sign in**: that is `DummyAuthenticator`, the template default.
  Replace it in `hub/jupyterhub_config.py` and rebuild before any real use.

## Still stuck?

Open an issue at
[the jupyter-positron-server issue tracker](https://github.com/posit-dev/jupyter-positron-server/issues)
with the relevant Hub and single-user log excerpts, your Positron Server version,
and which setup path you used.
